transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Start time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Markus Lee (Galactic Payments - Head of ML), Sofia Alvarez (Eng Manager), Ethan Park (Platform), Nora Kim (Product)

[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. quick agenda, we want to run through Optimize recommendations specifically around batching and our prefix / KV cache approach and then walk through a simple cost model and next steps. priya's going to demo some console views and the cost calc.
[00:00:22] Markus: Sounds good, our main thing is cost but we also can't sacrifice our p95 latency, payments chat is sensitive. we usually need sub-300ms p95 for user facing flows.
[00:00:35] Priya: got it, thanks for that context, and if you can, share the typical prompt sizes afterwards, that will help us tune batch sizes. from what Alex shared we saw you have spikey traffic, lots of short sessions.
[00:00:48] Sofia: yea many sessions are like 2-3 turns total, average tokens per request around 120, but some longer refund/chargebacks threads are 600+ tokens.
[00:01:05] Ethan: infra note - we run in GCP us-west2 and are evaluating a private deployment for compliance, we need to know if KV cache can run in our VPC or if it's hosted only.
[00:01:20] Alex: good question, KV cache in Redwood's Dedicated and Private modes can run in customer VPC - we can deploy cache nodes in the VPC, with KMS integrations and audit logs. for hosted there is a managed cache but we can discuss data retention controls.
[00:01:38] [00:01:40] Priya: ok jumping into the high level: batching increases GPU utilization by grouping concurrent tokens, so you get higher throughput at a small latency tail impact. there's continuous batching in our runtime which adaptively adjusts batch windows based on inter-arrival times.
[00:01:56] Markus: can you quantify "small latency tail impact"? our SLO is tight.
[00:02:05] Priya: sure. typical trade: moving from no batching to a conservative batch window (5-10ms) can reduce per-token cost ~15-25% with ~5-15ms p95 increase. aggressive batching (20-40ms window) can push cost savings to 30-45% but may add 30-60ms to p95 in worst cases. those numbers are workload dependent - hence the benchmark.
[00:02:32] [00:02:34] Liam: i'll add that batching is request-size aware; for your 120-token average requests we tend to group several onto a single GPU invocation, amortizing KV cache and softmax compute.
[00:02:46] Sofia: ok that's reasonable for background jobs, but user-facing flows need lower latency - can we do hybrid?
[00:02:54] Priya: yes, hybrid routing is common: low-latency route for interactive sessions (small batch window, p99 optimized), and a cost-optimized route for non-urgent flows. Redwood routing can do it by policy: user flag, route by rate, or canary percent.
[00:03:10] [00:03:12] Alex: now prefix vs KV cache - quickly: prefix cache stores whole prefix embeddings or token sequences keyed by user/session; KV cache stores keys & values for transformer layers to restore attention state. prefix cache is very good for repeated queries or templates, KV cache helps long session performance by avoiding recompute across tokens.
[00:03:31] Markus: i thought KV cache would be the same as prefix - what's the difference in practice?
[00:03:37] Priya: common confusion - prefix cache avoids re-encoding the prompt, i.e., you reuse the first n tokens. KV cache stores the attention keys/values after several decoder steps so new tokens don't need recomputing older attention operations. for autoregressive models KV cache can reduce compute for long sequences significantly.
[00:03:58] [00:04:00] Priya: in practice for your workflow: many sessions are short, but you have a minority of long sessions (refund investigations at 600 tokens). KV cache helps those long sessions the most. prefix cache helps when you have repeated structured prompts (e.g., same template for support responses).
[00:04:17] Ethan: will KV cache be hot in memory long term? how much memory for our 100k daily users?
[00:04:24] Liam: memory scales with active sessions and sequence length and model size. we typically evict cold sessions after configurable TTL (e.g., 5-30 minutes). we can size nodes and show cost impact in the model.
[00:04:36] [00:04:38] Priya: switching to the cost model slide - basic inputs: qps, avg tokens per request, cache hit rate, model cost per GPU-second, batch efficiency improvements. example: baseline no-cache, no-batching: 100 qps, 120 tokens/request => X tokens/sec -> cost Y. with moderate batching + 40% cache hit the per-token cost drops by ~35% in our example.
[00:04:58] Sofia: can you show the spreadsheet?
[00:05:02] Priya: sure sharing screen now - ok, top row is our assumptions. i see you sent us average token distribution earlier, that's helpful.
[00:05:12] [00:05:14] Priya: example numbers: model run cost per 1M tokens baseline $80 (this is illustrative), with conservative batching it becomes $64, with 40% KV hit it drops to $42. that is in part because each cache hit avoids forward passes over prefix or repeated tokens.
[00:05:33] Markus: that looks promising. what's a realistic KV hit for us - 40% seems optimistic?
[00:05:40] Priya: depends - for templates and repeated confirmation messages hit rates can be 50-70%. but across all flows, realistic initial expectation is 15-30% until you tune templates and session reuse. our Optimize consultant can help craft caching keys to increase effective hit rate.
[00:05:58] [00:06:00] Alex: also worth noting prefix cache and KV cache are additive in some cases - you can cache the prefix embedding and also maintain KV for ongoing decoding.
[00:06:09] Nora: security question - if we run KV cache in our VPC will token data be stored in cleartext in memory? any encryption at rest?
[00:06:18] Alex: KV cache nodes in your VPC will not write to disk by default; in Dedicated/Private mode we integrate with your KMS, and audit logs are available. we can configure memory encryption on supported instances and use HSM for keys if required. we'll include SOC2 artifacts in the packet.
[00:06:36] [00:06:38] Priya: going back to latency: in our benchmark template we measure p50/p95/p99 and token-level throughput. recommended canary: run a 2-hour test that mirrors your production distribution: 70% short chats, 30% long investigations. we can run both hosted dedicated and private configs to compare.
[00:06:58] Ethan: about routing - if we use hosted then fallback to dedicated under load, how seamless is that?
[00:07:05] Liam: Redwood routing supports fallback policies; we ensure model-variant compatibility and KV sync semantics are preserved if you use compatible model variants. warm-up penalties exist so for extremely latency-sensitive traffic you might pin to Dedicated nodes.
[00:07:20] [00:07:22] Priya: demo time - console screenshot: Optimize tab shows recommended batch window, estimated cost delta, and a simulated p95 impact given your supplied distribution. note small transcription: sometimes console label readouts showed "KV cash" in older logs - ignore that, it's a small OCR slip in the emailed pdf.
[00:07:40] Sofia: haha ok. can you export that report?
[00:07:43] Priya: yep - exportable CSV and shareable link.
[00:07:48] [00:07:50] Alex: now some practical recommendations for Galactic: 1) start with conservative batching (5-10ms) for interactive traffic to capture 15-20% cost savings with minimal p95 change; 2) enable KV cache for investigation flows and set TTL to 15min; 3) instrument cache hit metrics and have a 2-week tuning window to raise hit rates; 4) use hybrid routing: interactive low-latency pool + cost-optimized pool for non-critical flows.
[00:08:14] Markus: ok what about hardware - which GPU families are recommended?
[00:08:18] Liam: for your mix we'd recommend A10G or A100 depending on model size; for cost-sensitive medium models we often pick A10G in Dedicated; for highest throughput and large models A100 or H100 are typical. we'll size the fleet in the benchmark.
[00:08:31] [00:08:33] Priya: note quantization and kernel selection also matter; quantizing to 4-bit or 8-bit can reduce memory and increase batch sizes but needs eval to ensure no regression. we'll include quantization suggestions in the Optimize runbook.
[00:08:47] Sofia: any gotchas for inference determinism or slight output drift when using caching?
[00:08:53] Priya: caching does not change model weights but can change temperature of runtime due to different batching micro-timings; we haven't seen semantic regressions attributable to batching or KV cache, but we recommend perf + quality tests in the benchmark to ensure rollout safety.
[00:09:06] [00:09:08] Alex: ok wrapping up - quick recap. Alex to send pricing and the cost model, Priya to share runbook and KV cache whitepaper, schedule 2-hour benchmark week of 3/23, customer to provide dataset and prompt distribution.
[00:09:25] Markus: sounds good. one last question: do you support per-route token-level billing and tracing so we can attribute cost to product buckets?
[00:09:34] Liam: yes console provides per-route and per-model token breakdowns and trace hooks; we'll show an example in the benchmark report.
[00:09:44] [00:09:46] Sofia: thanks everyone - excited to try the benchmark.
[00:09:50] Alex: thanks, we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.
